Ui.Script:
-- The naming contract every verb below rests on: an "item button" is a Button whose own -- name prefixes its regions — `<name>IconTexture`, `<name>Count`, `<name>Stock`, -- `<name>NormalTexture`, `<name>NameFrame`, `<name>SlotTexture`. That is the reference's -- `$parent…` template shape, and it is why these are free functions taking a button rather -- than widget methods: any button that follows the naming works, whoever built it. -- -- TWO DIFFERENT NILS, and the difference is the whole error policy of this file. -- A nil BUTTON is a no-op everywhere: callers hand us whatever their loop is holding, and -- the reference tolerates that in all eight verbs, so we do too. A button that is missing -- the REGION is not tolerated — the lookup yields nil and the very next `:` raises. That -- loudness is deliberate: "this is not an item button" is a real mistake by the caller, and -- 1203's lesson is that the silent version of a failure is the expensive one.
-- One named region off a button, which is the only address these verbs ever compute. Nil in, -- nil out, so the button guard reads as one expression instead of eight copied early -- returns. local function region(button, suffix) return button and getglobal(button:GetName() .. suffix) end
-- Four of the eight differ in nothing but which region they tint, so they share the verb -- and name the region. The guard is on the BUTTON and deliberately not on the region it -- resolved: a nil button is the tolerated case, a button carrying no such region is the -- loud one. `texture` is a local rather than an inline call only so that the raise names -- which lookup came back empty. local function tint(button, suffix, r, g, b) local texture = region(button, suffix) if button then texture:SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end end
function SetItemButtonCount(button, count) if not button then return end count = count or 0 button.count = count local label = region(button, "Count") -- `isBag` is the reference's own flag for a bag button, where even a single item -- counts as a number worth showing. Above 999 the slot shows a bare `*` — the stack -- is "more than the label can say" — while `button.count` keeps the real number. if count > 1 or (button.isBag and count > 0) then label:SetText(count > 999 and "*" or count) label:Show() else label:Hide() end end
function SetItemButtonStock(button, numInStock) if not button then return end -- The reference defaults this to `""` and then compares it with `> 0`, which is a -- string/number comparison Lua refuses — a raise on the only path the default can -- reach. Ours defaults to 0, which is what the branch below actually means. Not aping -- a quirk (method step 3); the behaviour on every reachable path is identical. numInStock = numInStock or 0 button.numInStock = numInStock local label = region(button, "Stock") if numInStock > 0 then label:SetText(format(MERCHANT_STOCK, numInStock)) label:Show() else label:Hide() end end
function SetItemButtonTexture(button, texture) if not button then return end local icon = region(button, "IconTexture") -- Visibility tracks the ARGUMENT, not the region's contents, and it is settled before -- the texture is assigned: clearing a slot with a nil texture must leave the region -- hidden, never an empty quad standing where the icon was. if texture then icon:Show() else icon:Hide() end icon:SetTexture(texture) end
function SetItemButtonTextureVertexColor(button, r, g, b) tint(button, "IconTexture", r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonNormalTextureVertexColor(button, r, g, b) tint(button, "NormalTexture", r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonNameFrameVertexColor(button, r, g, b) tint(button, "NameFrame", r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonSlotVertexColor(button, r, g, b) tint(button, "SlotTexture", r, g, b) end
function SetItemButtonDesaturated(button, desaturated, r, g, b) -- The one verb whose own nil guard is on the ICON rather than the button: the -- reference checks both, and `region()` collapses them into this single test without -- changing which calls no-op and which raise. local icon = region(button, "IconTexture") if not icon then return end -- The reference asks the texture itself whether the desaturating shader is available -- (`local shaderSupported = icon:SetDesaturated(desaturated)`) and falls through to a -- flat grey tint when it is not — 1.12 ran on fixed-function hardware where that was -- the ordinary answer. Since decision 1327 benilla's answer is YES: the icon greys to -- luminance in the shader and wears the caller's own tint on top, which is what the -- ref's own `(1, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65)` and `(locked, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)` calls are asking -- for. The `icon.SetDesaturated and` guard stays for a region leaf without the verb; -- the flat-grey arm below is then the ref's own fallback, unchanged. local shaderSupported = icon.SetDesaturated and icon:SetDesaturated(desaturated) -- Undesaturated is full colour whatever the caller passed; desaturated is the caller's -- own tint when they named one AND the shader took it, and the flat grey otherwise. if not desaturated then r, g, b = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 elseif not r or not shaderSupported then r, g, b = 0.5, 0.5, 0.5 end icon:SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end
